fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is MoS2 addition to bare CoCrFeNi, whereas the target intervention varies Mo content in an existing CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.

The claim of improved friction and wear throughout room temperature to 800 °C is unsupported by E1, which concerns a different AlCoCrFeNiTi system and does not establish performance across the full stated range.
The mechanism assumes MoS2 remains lubricious at high temperature in air but omits its oxidation and the target's essential Ag-containing molybdate/oxide glaze mechanism.
The proposed baseline lacks Ni-coated MoS2, Ag, Cr2O3, and baseline Mo, preventing a meaningful reconstruction of the target comparison.
The falsification rule permits failure at much of the temperature range as long as improvement occurs in three conditions, so it does not test the claimed full-range effectiveness.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad tribological problem and proposes a single, testable intervention, but it does not reconstruct the studied material or intervention. It captures only the low-shear MoS2 mechanism relevant at lower temperatures and misses Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, and high-temperature NiO/silver-molybdate glaze formation. Test conditions are underspecified with respect to load, speed, distance, counterface, and environment. E1 supports incorporating roughly 10 wt.% MoS2 into a different HEA at limited temperatures, but cannot justify efficacy in CoCrFeNi through 800 °C or under varying loads and environments. The controlled comparison is useful in principle, though its falsification criterion is inconsistent with the universal full-range prediction.
